Rashi on Ketubot 75a:11:1.english: That is positioned on her forehead - And still, [it is] where there is no hair on it and [it is] small.

Rashi on Ketubot 75a:12:1.english: And its place became a scar - [Meaning] that a mark remained there after the wound healed.

Rashi on Ketubot 75a:12:2.hebrew: צלקת - פינדרור"א. ודוגמתה בשחיטת חולין (דף קכד.) גבי תנור כלי חרס, דצלקיה מצלק:
Rashi on Ketubot 75a:12:2.english: A scar - [In Old French:] *fendrure* [a crack/fissure]. And its parallel is in Shechitat Chullin (124a) regarding an oven [that is] an earthenware vessel, [where it states] *detzalkei mitzlak* [that it is cracked].

Rashi on Ketubot 75a:12:3.hebrew: למעליותא - והכי קאמר: נוי הוא לאשה שיהו דדיה מובדלים טפח:
Rashi on Ketubot 75a:12:3.english: For perfection - And this is what he means: It is a beauty for a woman that her breasts be separated by a handbreadth.

Rashi on Ketubot 75a:12:4.hebrew: גבי מומין תניא - הך מתני' גבי מומין תניא, דקא חשיב זיעה ושומא וריח הפה ושאר מומין, וטפח בין שני דדי אשה:
Rashi on Ketubot 75a:12:4.english: It is taught with regard to blemishes - This baraita is taught with regard to blemishes, as it enumerates sweat, a mole, bad breath, and the other blemishes, and a handbreadth between a woman's two breasts.

Rashi on Ketubot 75a:12:5.english: And how much - [is] beauty for her?

Rashi on Ketubot 75a:13:1.english: And how much - [must] they be larger than those of other [women] for it to be a blemish?

Rashi on Ketubot 75a:14:1.hebrew: ולציון יאמר - משום דאיירי בה רבי מיישא, נקיט לה. "ולציון יאמר איש ואיש יולד בה" — לעתיד לבא, כשיתקיים מקרא שכתוב "והביאו את כל אחיכם מנחה לה' וגו'", כל מקום שימצאו שם ישראל יאמרו העמים: "זהו מבני ציון, זה יולד בה, נביאנו שם":
Rashi on Ketubot 75a:14:1.english: And of Zion it shall be said - Because Rabbi Meyasha spoke about it, [the Gemara] cites it. "And of Zion it shall be said, this man and this man were born in her" — in the future, when the verse that is written, "And they shall bring all your brethren [as] an offering to the Lord, etc.," is fulfilled, wherever they find Jews there, the nations will say: "This one is from the children of Zion; this one was born in her — let us bring him there."

Rashi on Ketubot 75a:14:2.english: And of Zion - Like, "And the men of the place asked of his wife" (Genesis 26:7), [meaning] "about his wife."

Rashi on Ketubot 75a:14:3.english: And He will establish her, the Most High - The Holy One, Blessed be He, will establish her to be supreme, above the entire world.

Rashi on Ketubot 75a:14:4.hebrew: אחד הנולד בה כו' - "איש איש" יתירא קא דריש: אחד הנולד בה ואחד המצפה לראותה, יקרא מבניה ויביאוהו אצלה:
Rashi on Ketubot 75a:14:4.english: One who was born in her, etc. - He expounds the superfluous [repetition of] "man [and] man" [to teach that] one who was born in her and one who looks forward to seeing her will [both] be called among her children, and they will bring him to her.

Rashi on Ketubot 75a:14:5.english: And one of them - Of the inhabitants of the Land of Israel.

Rashi on Ketubot 75a:14:6.english: Is superior - [They are] clever and sharp.

Rashi on Ketubot 75a:15:1.english: The father must bring proof - If he comes to claim a ketubah from the betrothal from this [groom] who refuses to take her [in marriage].

Rashi on Ketubot 75a:15:2.hebrew: נכנסה לרשות הבעל - ניסת, והוא בא להוציאה בלא כתובה על מומין שבה:
Rashi on Ketubot 75a:15:2.english: She entered the husband's domain - [That is,] she was married, and he comes to divorce her without [paying her] ketubah because of blemishes that are on her.

Rashi on Ketubot 75a:15:3.hebrew: הבעל צריך להביא ראיה - עדים, וכולה מפרש בגמרא:
Rashi on Ketubot 75a:15:3.english: The husband must bring proof - Witnesses; and all of it is explained in the Gemara.

Rashi on Ketubot 75a:15:4.english: In what [case] are [these] things said - that the husband can make a claim regarding the blemishes.

Rashi on Ketubot 75a:1:1.english: And the children of Israel did not smite them - [This] is written regarding the Gibeonites.

Rashi on Ketubot 75a:3:1.english: Rava said - [This refers to] that which [the baraita] teaches: "[If she went] to a sage and he dissolved her [vow], she is not betrothed."

Rashi on Ketubot 75a:3:2.hebrew: באשה חשובה - בת גדולים. דאפי' למ"ד רוצה אדם שתתבזה אשתו בב"ד, הכא אמר אי אפשי באשה נדרנית, וגט נמי לא ניחא לי למיתבא לה דאתסר באמה ואחותה, ולא ניחא לי דליהוו קדושין:
Rashi on Ketubot 75a:3:2.english: With an important woman - A daughter of prominent [people]. For even according to the one who says a man wants his wife to be disgraced in court, here he says: "I do not want a vow-making wife, and it is also not amenable to me to give her a bill of divorce [such] that I become forbidden to her mother and her sister; and [thus] it is not amenable to me that [this] should be a [valid] betrothal."

Rashi on Ketubot 75a:4:1.english: But he - If he said to her, "On condition that there are no blemishes or vows upon me."

Rashi on Ketubot 75a:5:1.hebrew: טן דו - גוף שנים. משל הדיוט הוא, שהנשים אומרות: טוב לשבת עם גוף שנים משבת אלמנה:
Rashi on Ketubot 75a:5:1.english: Tan du - [Meaning] a body of two. It is a common proverb that women say: "It is better to sit with a body of two than to sit [as] a widow."

Rashi on Ketubot 75a:5:2.hebrew: דשומשמנא גברא - משל הדיוט הוא, מי שבעלה קטן כנמלה:
Rashi on Ketubot 75a:5:2.english: [One] whose husband is an ant - It is a common proverb, [meaning] one whose husband is small as an ant.

Rashi on Ketubot 75a:5:3.hebrew: כורסיה בי חראתא רמיא - כסאה בין השרות, בנות חורין, מושיבה, כלומר: גם לי בעל כמוכם:
Rashi on Ketubot 75a:5:3.english: She places her seat among the noblewomen - She sets her chair among the princesses, freeborn women, as if to say: "I too have a husband like you."

Rashi on Ketubot 75a:6:1.hebrew: נפסא - מנפס צמר, ואומנות מאוסה היא:
Rashi on Ketubot 75a:6:1.english: Nafsa - A wool comber, and it is a repulsive occupation.

Rashi on Ketubot 75a:6:2.english: She calls him at the threshold of the door and sits - She is not ashamed to call him to the threshold of the house to sit there beside him in front of everyone.

Rashi on Ketubot 75a:6:3.english: Kulsa - [One who is] from a disreputable family.

Rashi on Ketubot 75a:6:4.hebrew: טלפחי - עדשים, שהוא מאכל קל ואין חסרון כיס כל כך, אינה שואלת הימנו, אך יקרא שמו עליה:
Rashi on Ketubot 75a:6:4.english: Telafchei - Lentils, which are a light food and [involve] not so much financial loss, she does not ask from him, [desiring] only that his name be called upon her.

Rashi on Ketubot 75a:6:5.hebrew: וכולן מזנות ותולות בבעליהן - כל אלו שבעליהן שפלים ומראות להם חבה, אינו אלא שמזנות תחתיהן, וכשמתעברות, הן תולות את העובר בבעל [ונוח להן באנשים כל שהן, לפי שמזנות תחתיהן]:
Rashi on Ketubot 75a:6:5.english: And all of them commit adultery and attribute [it] to their husbands - All those [women] whose husbands are lowly yet show them affection, it is only because they commit adultery while married to them, and when they conceive, they attribute the fetus to the husband [and they are content with any men whatsoever, because they commit adultery while married to them].

Rashi on Ketubot 75a:7:1.english: They added to them - [Regarding] women, [blemishes] that are not [disqualifying] in priests.

Rashi on Ketubot 75a:7:3.english: A mole [shuma] - Verrue [in Old French] (verrue: a wart).

Rashi on Ketubot 75a:7:4.hebrew: הזקן והחולה והמזוהם - לגבי מומי בהמה תנן, וקס"ד זיעה וריח הפה דאדם בכלל מזוהם:
Rashi on Ketubot 75a:7:4.english: The old, the sick, and the filthy - We learned [this] regarding blemishes of an animal, and we initially assumed [that] sweat and [foul] odor of the mouth of a person are included in "filthy."

Rashi on Ketubot 75a:9:1.hebrew: זיעה אמזוהם קא רמית - לאו רומיא היא. מזוהם גופו מסריח ובאדם נמי פוסל, אבל זיעה דאדם אינה פוסלת בכהנים, כדקתני הוסיפו עליהם:
Rashi on Ketubot 75a:9:1.english: Have you raised a contradiction [between] sweat [and] a filthy [one] - This is not a contradiction. "Filthy" [means] his body has a foul odor, and in a human [priest] as well it disqualifies [him], whereas human sweat does not disqualify priests, as it teaches: "They added to them."

Rashi on Ketubot 75a:9:2.hebrew: דאפשר לעברה בקיוהא דחמרא - ביין קהה, אייגר"א בלע"ז, עד שיעבוד עבודתו:
Rashi on Ketubot 75a:9:2.english: For it is possible to remove it with sour wine - With sour wine, aigre in Old French, until he performs his service.

Rashi on Ketubot 75a:9:3.hebrew: וריח הפה נמי כו' - אבל גבי אשה, שהוא מדבר עמה כל שעה, לא אפשר:
Rashi on Ketubot 75a:9:3.english: And odor of the mouth as well, etc. - But with regard to a woman, with whom he speaks at all times, it is not possible.

Tosafot on Ketubot 75a:15:1.hebrew: וחכמים אומרים בד"א במומין שבסתר כו' - נראה לרבינו יצחק דר"מ לא פליג אמומין שבגלוי, דמודה דאין יכול לטעון, דראה וניפייס הוא, כדאמר סתמא דהש"ס בגמרא. ועוד, דאי פליג אמומין שבגלוי, אם כן משכחת לה סימפון בעבדים במומין שבגלוי לר' מאיר, ולא פליג אלא ביש מרחץ:
Tosafot on Ketubot 75a:15:1.english: And the Sages say: In what [case] is this statement [said]? With regard to hidden blemishes, etc. - It appears to Rabbeinu Yitzchak that Rabbi Meir does not disagree regarding exposed blemishes, for he concedes that [the husband] cannot make a claim [regarding them], since he saw [them] and was reconciled, as the anonymous voice of the Talmud states in the Gemara. Furthermore, if he disagreed regarding exposed blemishes, then you would find [a case of] simpon [annulment due to a defect] in slaves with exposed blemishes according to Rabbi Meir; rather, he only disagrees where there is a bathhouse.

Tosafot on Ketubot 75a:4:1.hebrew: אי הכי סיפא דקתני אבל הוא שהלך כו' - דבשלמא אי טעמא משום דאין אדם רוצה שתתבזה אשתו בב"ד, בבעל לא שייך זילותא לילך, שרגיל ללכת בב"ד כל שעה לצרכו:
Tosafot on Ketubot 75a:4:1.english: If so, [consider] the latter clause which teaches: "But [if] he went," etc. - For it is well if the reason [in the first clause] is because a man does not want his wife to be disgraced in court; [with] a husband, disgrace does not apply to [his] going, as he is accustomed to go to court at all times for his needs.

Tosafot on Ketubot 75a:8:1.hebrew: כאן בזיעה עוברת - שיכול להעבירה ע"י רחיצת מים, דאכתי לא ידע דאפשר לעבורי בקיוהא דחמרא. דההיא לא פסלה בכהנים, שהעבודה לפי שעה הוא — אפשר שמרחיצה ועוברת. ואין לפרש "עוברת" שעשויה להתרפאות, דהיכי נוקי מתני' בשאינה עוברת? הא "בין קבועין בין עוברין" קתני! ועי"ל, דזיעה עוברת — שעשויה להתרפאות, ואפילו לא העבירה כשר לעבודה, דלא מאיסה כולי האי; ו"מזוהם" הוי דווקא זיעה שאינה עוברת. והא דקתני "בין קבועין בין עוברין", אכל מומין דקתני התם קאי, וה"פ: בין קבועין ששנויין באותה משנה, בין עוברין ששנויין שם, כגון חוורור:
Tosafot on Ketubot 75a:8:1.english: Here, [it is speaking] of removable sweat - That one can remove it by washing with water, for [the speaker] does not yet know that it can be removed with the acidity of wine. For that [kind of sweat] does not disqualify priests, since the [Temple] service is temporary — it is possible that he washes it [off] and it passes. And one should not explain "passing" [overet] as meaning that it is likely to heal, for [if so,] how could we establish the Mishnah as [referring to] that which does not pass? Behold, it teaches: "Whether permanent or passing"! And one can also say that "passing sweat" [means] that it is likely to heal, and even if he did not remove it, he is fit for [Temple] service, because it is not so repulsive; and "filthy" [mezoham] refers specifically to sweat that does not pass. And that which it teaches, "whether permanent or passing," refers to all the blemishes that are taught there, and this is its explanation: whether permanent [blemishes] that are taught in that Mishnah, or passing [blemishes] that are taught there, such as a white spot [on the eye].
